morning.description: Wake up gently. Vata types need more rest and should avoid rushing.
Drink warm water with a pinch of salt and lime.
Gentle, grounding yoga and slow walks.
Warm, nourishing breakfast like oatmeal or stewed apples.

afternoon.description: Heaviest meal of the day. Warm, moist, and grounding foods.
Short rest or meditation to ground excess Vata energy.

evening.description: Light, warm, and easily digestible meal (e.g., soups, stews).
Warm oil massage (Abhyanga), reading, or calming music.

night.description: In bed by 10 PM. Vata needs sufficient, deep sleep.

morning.description: Drink room temperature water or water with aloe vera/coriander.
Moderate exercise, swimming, or cooling yoga sequences.
Cooling, sweet, and satisfying breakfast (e.g., fruit bowl, toast).

afternoon.description: Substantial, cooling lunch with raw salads or sweet vegetables.
Take a short walk outdoors, ideally near water or in a garden.

evening.description: Moderate dinner avoiding excessively spicy or sour foods.
Relaxing activities, avoid intense discussions or screen time.

morning.description: Wake up early before sunrise to avoid sluggishness.
Drink warm water with honey and lemon/ginger.
Vigorous exercise, brisk walking, or active yoga (Sun Salutations).
Light breakfast or skip if not hungry. Fresh fruit or light tea.

afternoon.description: Warm, light, and spiced meal. Largest meal of the day.

evening.description: Very light dinner (e.g., vegetable soup) before 7 PM.

night.description: Kapha types need less sleep than Vata or Pitta.

morning.description: Drink warm or room temperature water.

night.description: Aim for 7-8 hours of restful sleep.

Spring.name: Vasanta (Spring)
Spring.adjustment: Spring is Kapha season. Focus on lighter diets, vigorous exercise, and warming spices to melt accumulated winter Kapha.

Summer.name: Grishma (Summer)
Summer.adjustment: Summer is Pitta season. Stay cool, favor sweet and astringent tastes, and avoid excessive sun exposure.

Autumn.name: Sharad (Autumn)
Autumn.adjustment: Autumn marks a transition. Begin incorporating grounding, warming foods to prepare for Vata season, while clearing summer Pitta.

Winter.name: Hemanta/Shishira (Winter)
Winter.adjustment: Winter is Vata season. Prioritize warm, heavy, unctuous foods and grounding routines to combat cold and dryness.
